在2024年的某个平凡日子，一款名为《香蕉》的游戏，以其荒诞到极致的内核，悄然攀上了Steam热门榜的巅峰——它没有剧情，没有玩法，唯一的交互是点击屏幕上一根不断生长的香蕉。这并非行为艺术，而是一场精心策划的、针对人性贪婪与互联网记忆的精准收割。它继承自2022年《羊了个羊》的社交裂变血统，却剥离了最后一丝伪装，将“庞氏游戏化”的底层逻辑赤裸裸地摊在阳光下：生产虚拟物品，并期待下一个出价更高者接盘。 而《香蕉与黄瓜》，这款姗姗来迟的模仿者，就像一场盛大葬礼结束后才匆匆赶到的吊唁者。它手捧更为粗制滥造的祭品——香蕉、黄瓜，以及那令人费解的“蕉瓜混合体”——茫然地站在已然冷却的坟场中央，不明白为何无人再为这些虚拟物品欢呼。 从表面上看，《香蕉与黄瓜》的设计简洁到足以写进教科书。其核心循环可以被概括为一个三步颂歌：第一步，生产。游戏操作简单到极致，如同一个最小化的点击闲置游戏。你需要点击香蕉与黄瓜来增加计数器，时间（每3-18小时）会随机掉落香蕉、黄瓜以及稀有变体如“蕉瓜混合体”。这里几乎没有技巧或策略，主要依赖时间兑换和随机掉落。它模仿了区块链世界“质押生息”的表面机制，却完全依赖Steam的内置系统，而非任何区块链技术或去中心化信任。第二步，确权与幻想。每一件掉落的香蕉、黄瓜，都庄严地躺在你的Steam库存里。这套设计，直接借鉴自NFT（非同质化代币）那套“赋予虚拟物品稀缺性和独特性”的理念。它试图让你相信，你拥有的不是一行代码生成的图片，而是有“稀缺性”和“市场价值”的“资产”。这是整个游戏设计中最精妙的心理引导。第三步，交易与击鼓传花。你可以将你的“资产”挂牌到Steam社区市场，标上一个你梦想中的价格。至此，游戏的真实目的浮出水面：它不注重点击的乐趣，而更依赖你心中那团名为“或许有人会高价买入”的期望之火。整个游戏的生命，都维系于这个市场能否持续响起交易的叮咚声。这构成了一个完美的、自循环的金融幻梦模拟器。它用游戏的外衣，包装了一个最古老的投机故事。 如果说《香蕉》中那些各种各样的香蕉图还带着一丝艺术设计感（其中一些稀有且外表漂亮的香蕉价格更是水涨船高，部分玩家甚至认为这样的香蕉有收藏和展示价值），那么《香蕉与黄瓜》的美术，则是一场彻头彻尾的灾难。它甚至没能达到前辈那种“可收藏”的水准。这种粗糙，更像是一种玩世不恭的宣言。它仿佛在嘲弄玩家：“看，我们连假装认真做美术都觉得多余，但这不影响你们来追逐利润，对吧？”这种极致敷衍的美学，消解了这种虚拟物品最后一丝作为“收藏品”或“艺术品”的想象空间，将其纯粹的功能性（作为投机标的）暴露无遗。当承载价值的容器本身已毫无价值感时，里面的内容又能价值几何？ 所有的问题，最终都汇聚于那个寂静如死的市场。这不是暂时性的流动性枯竭，而是一级市场彻底关闭后的必然终局。《香蕉与黄瓜》犯下了无可救药的时机错误。它诞生于一个叙事已然彻底破产的周期末尾。它所效仿的《香蕉》、《猫》，乃至更早的《蛋》，已经完成了一场完整的“叙事炒作—涌入—流动性峰值—泡沫破裂—信仰崩塌”的标准周期。最早一批相信“点击即赚钱”的冒险家与傻瓜，早已在上一轮牛熊转换中被彻底清洗。剩余的，要么是伤痕累累、警惕性极高的老韭菜，要么是冷眼旁观、等待下一个热点的猎手。此时入场，《香蕉与黄瓜》面对的是一片早已被反复犁过、养分耗尽的盐碱地。它试图向已经学会看财务报表（尽管是虚假的）的观众，兜售一个画得更差的小丑戏法。当没有新的、更傻的资本来接盘，这个依靠纯粹信心（或者说贪婪）维持的金字塔，便只剩下一个结局：所有后来者挂在市场上的香蕉、黄瓜和蕉瓜混合体，都成了无人问津的数字墓碑，静静地记录着持有者投入的时间与最后落空的期望。收益？那是一个存在于宣传语和先行者故事里的、遥远的神话。 在这款游戏中没有赚到钱的我，在写测评时的心情是极其愤怒的。我的愤怒，并非源于“没有赚到钱”——游戏玩家本不应将个人投资损益带入游戏评价。真正的愤怒，源于这款游戏对“游戏”二字的亵渎，以及对玩家智商的极度蔑视。它将游戏设计最核心的“心流体验”、“挑战反馈”、“叙事共情”等元素全部剥离，只留下最原始的斯金纳箱操作（点击-奖励）和金融赌场预期（挂售-暴富）。它不提供任何审美愉悦、智力挑战或情感波动，只提供一种名为“等待暴富”的慢性焦虑。当预期落空，这种焦虑便迅速转化为被戏弄的怒火。更令人不齿的是，这类纯粹金融化、零和博弈甚至负和博弈的“游戏”扭曲了整个市场对“游戏价值”的评判标准。它让投机取代了创意，让传花鼓声掩盖了玩法迭代的号角。《香蕉与黄瓜》不仅仅是一款失败的游戏，它更是一个标志着某个荒谬泡沫已到强弩之末的、迟来的墓碑。它用自身的存在证明：当一种模式连最拙劣的模仿者都无法养活时，它的生命故事就已经写到了最后一页。它留给行业的唯一“价值”，或许就是作为未来教科书中的一个经典反面案例：看，这就是在错误的时间，以最低劣的品质，闯入一个已彻底腐烂的市场，所能得到的全部结局——除了开发者服务器账单上微不足道的电费，和玩家库存里一串永不成交的冰冷代码，一无所有。 优点： 1. 游戏操作简单，三岁小孩子都会玩，只要打开它每过一段时间就会掉落香蕉和黄瓜，还有一半是黄瓜一半是香蕉的蕉瓜混合体。 2. 掉落的香蕉、黄瓜、蕉瓜混合体可以挂到市场中去卖，如果有傻子愿意买你的香蕉、黄瓜、蕉瓜混合体，你就会赚到钱。 3. 有多种多样的香蕉、黄瓜、蕉瓜混合体掉落。 缺点： 1. 这个市场已经死了，没人买香蕉、黄瓜、蕉瓜混合体了。 2. 香蕉、黄瓜、蕉瓜混合体看着就是粗制滥造的，其图片质量甚至还不如蛋。 3. 这蠢游戏是在蛋、蕉、猫快要凉的时候才跟风出的，这个时候相信自己可以在这个市场赚大钱的傻子早就没剩几个了。因此掉落的香蕉、黄瓜、蕉瓜混合体根本没有傻子愿意接盘，我在这个游戏里赚到的钱连一毛都没有，收益远远少于蛋、蕉、猫。

Banana & Cucumber is an absurdly minimalistic free-to-play clicker game that perfectly represents the strange intersection between internet meme culture, idle gameplay addiction, and Steam marketplace economics. Developed by cem99 and slh99 and published by Bull Games, the title revolves around an intentionally ridiculous concept where players repeatedly click on a banana and cucumber to generate collectible item drops. At first glance, the game appears almost like a parody of modern clicker games, and in many ways that is exactly what it is. However, beneath the simplicity lies a surprisingly fascinating social experiment driven less by gameplay and more by digital collectibles, community speculation, and ironic entertainment. The gameplay loop is intentionally stripped down to the bare minimum. Players launch the game and immediately begin clicking on giant fruit icons in order to generate additional bananas, cucumbers, and item drops tied to the Steam marketplace system. There are no traditional objectives, combat systems, levels, puzzles, or meaningful progression mechanics in the conventional sense. The entire experience revolves around repetition, passive engagement, and waiting for valuable item drops to appear. The simplicity is so extreme that it almost becomes comedic, and the game clearly understands the absurdity of its own design. What makes Banana & Cucumber more interesting than its mechanics would normally allow is the Steam marketplace integration. Players receive random cosmetic drops and collectible items that can be traded or sold through Steam’s community marketplace. Some items remain essentially worthless, while others occasionally gain speculative value depending on rarity and community interest. This transforms the act of endlessly clicking fruit into a strange form of marketplace-driven anticipation where players continue interacting with the game primarily for the possibility of receiving rare or profitable drops. The game’s popularity stems less from traditional entertainment and more from the bizarre ecosystem surrounding it. Similar to other viral idle clicker titles on Steam, Banana & Cucumber became part of a wider online discussion about digital item economies, low-effort game design, and the strange psychology of passive progression systems. Many players participate ironically, treating the game as a joke or meme experiment rather than a serious gaming experience. Others become invested in item collecting, market speculation, and event participation despite the almost nonexistent gameplay depth. One of the game’s most amusing qualities is how self-aware it feels. Banana & Cucumber never pretends to offer a deep narrative or mechanically rich experience. Instead, it fully embraces internet absurdity and meme culture. The humor comes directly from the sheer meaninglessness of the gameplay itself. Clicking endlessly on oversized fruit while waiting for random item drops becomes strangely hypnotic precisely because the game openly acknowledges how pointless the activity really is. Visually, the game adopts an intentionally simplistic and low-budget presentation. Menus are minimal, animations are basic, and much of the visual identity revolves around exaggerated fruit imagery and meme aesthetics. According to the Steam page, certain visuals are AI-generated, which further reinforces the strange internet-driven atmosphere surrounding the game. Rather than polished graphics or artistic depth, the presentation relies entirely on novelty and absurd humor. The sound design is similarly minimalistic. Audio feedback exists mainly to reinforce the repetitive clicking loop rather than create immersion or atmosphere. Music and sound effects are extremely basic because the game is designed more as a passive background activity than a fully engaging gameplay experience. Many players likely leave the game running while multitasking rather than actively focusing on it for long periods. Community interaction plays a surprisingly important role in sustaining player interest. The developers organize Discord events and community activities that allow players to obtain exclusive item drops and participate in the strange collector-driven culture surrounding the game. This creates a dedicated ecosystem of traders, collectors, meme participants, and curious players who treat the title almost like an ongoing social phenomenon rather than a conventional game. However, the game’s biggest weakness is also its entire identity: there is almost no actual gameplay depth. Outside of clicking and collecting items, there are virtually no meaningful systems to engage with. Players searching for strategy, challenge, storytelling, or progression beyond marketplace speculation will likely lose interest quickly. The experience depends almost entirely on novelty and curiosity to maintain engagement. The game also exists within a controversial space on Steam. Many players and online discussions criticize titles like Banana & Cucumber for encouraging marketplace farming and speculative behavior rather than genuine entertainment value. Some view the game as harmless meme-driven fun, while others see it as an example of low-effort releases exploiting digital item economies and player psychology. This controversy has become part of the game’s identity and significantly shapes how people perceive it. The repetitive nature of the gameplay also becomes impossible to ignore over time. Once the novelty fades, players are left with an experience built almost entirely around repetition and passive waiting. Unlike stronger idle games that introduce evolving systems and progression mechanics, Banana & Cucumber intentionally remains shallow. Whether this becomes frustrating or amusing depends entirely on the player’s tolerance for absurdist humor and minimal interaction. Despite all of these criticisms, the game succeeds remarkably well at being exactly what it intends to be. Banana & Cucumber is not trying to become an emotionally deep indie masterpiece or a mechanically complex simulation. It exists as a bizarre internet curiosity fueled by memes, digital marketplaces, and ironic participation. Its strange appeal comes directly from how unapologetically pointless it feels. What ultimately makes the game memorable is the unusual social environment surrounding it. The combination of idle clicking, Steam item speculation, meme culture, and passive engagement creates something that feels uniquely tied to modern online gaming culture. In many ways, the game functions less as a traditional entertainment product and more as a commentary on digital economies and internet-driven trends. Banana & Cucumber may offer almost no meaningful gameplay depth, but it still stands out as one of the stranger examples of modern Steam culture. Players interested in internet oddities, experimental clicker games, or marketplace-driven meme phenomena may find it strangely compelling despite its extreme simplicity and lack of substance. Rating: 5/10
